title: The Man who Never Laughed

full_text:
In Baghdad lived a handsome, wealthy youth who, through profligate living, squandered his inheritance and was reduced to serving ten venerable old men who dwelt together in a magnificent mansion. The ten elders were dressed in perpetual black mourning robes, weeping and lamenting every evening, but none would ever reveal the cause of their sorrow.

They exacted one solemn condition from the young servant: 'Serve us faithfully, ask no questions concerning our tears, and above all, never seek to open the golden door at the end of the courtyard.'

For twelve years, the youth served them with devotion, watching the elders pass away one by one until only he remained master of the grand mansion.

Left alone, the forbidden golden door began to torment his thoughts day and night. At last, consumed by reckless curiosity, he turned the golden key, pushed open the portal, and stepped into an enchanted garden.

A giant bird of emerald plumage seized him by the shoulders, carried him across oceans of clouds, and deposited him in a paradisiacal kingdom where a peerless Queen crowned him her sovereign and husband.

'All this kingdom is yours,' said the Queen with tender love, 'rejoice with me forever, but on your life, never touch the ebony door at the foot of our garden terrace.'

For thirty days the youth lived in bliss. But the itch of forbidden curiosity seized him once again: he unlocked the ebony door!

Instantly, the giant emerald bird appeared, seized him by his sash, carried him through the clouds, and hurled him back onto the dusty floor of the Baghdad courtyard!

The golden door was sealed forever, leaving the youth to don black robes and spend the remainder of his days weeping among the empty halls, known to all as the man who never laughed again.
moral: Unbridled curiosity that breaks solemn prohibitions destroys paradise and leaves a lifetime of sorrow.
